name: Hakuto-R Mission 1
left: Crash debris (April 2023), with the Rashid and SORA-Q rovers it carried
fact: Japanese company ispace launched its first lander on 11 December 2022 and flew a slow, low-energy route that took it 1.38 million km from Earth before it entered lunar orbit on 21 March 2023. On 25 April 2023 the braking went as planned, but passing a crater rim about 3 km high the altitude reading jumped; the software rejected the altimeter and believed the lander was on the ground while it was still about 5 km up. It descended slowly until its propellant ran out, then fell. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter found the debris.
capability: Eight of its ten mission milestones were met before the landing. ispace traced the loss to software and to a simulation that left out the terrain on the approach path, not to the hardware.
